Episode summary: Participants recommend structured databases because future cross-run questions cannot be anticipated.
Consequence / analytical outcome: A concise final report is insufficient for longitudinal analysis
Coding note: Positive pattern: structured retention enables later diagnosis.

Episode summary: Tip pickup and aspiration complete before a destination-lid state error prevents dispensing.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Valuable liquid remains in tips and state must be restored manually
Coding note: Canonical irreversible-prefix episode.

Episode summary: Discussion considers assertions, prevalidation, and queuing the operation sequence to expose modeled-state errors before dispatch.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Some partial-execution failures may be preventable before physical action
Coding note: Positive design direction; implementation outcome not confirmed.

Episode summary: Participants distinguish errors detectable from common state from firmware-format and backend-specific errors.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Not every failure can be shifted into compile-time or simulation checks
Coding note: Supports detection-layer coding. B2 modifier removed: the interface works, and the episode is about which layer can detect an error rather than about reaching the device.

Episode summary: The initial multi-user scenario specifies devices, capacities, and durations but omits scientific disposition and timing constraints.
Consequence / analytical outcome: No exact schedule can be judged from the stated information
Coding note: Denominator for Constraint Completeness becomes explicit.

Episode summary: Replies add assay timing, storage tolerance, interruptibility, priorities, disposal, and whether samples can remain in particular devices.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Scientific constraints determine feasible schedules
Coding note: Strong context-expansion pattern outside AI.

Episode summary: A participant proposes a standardized method for naming assets, processes, timings, dependencies, and priorities.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Comparable scheduling requires a shared input representation
Coding note: Positive contribution emerging from an underdetermined toy problem.

Episode summary: Discussion notes that even advanced workcells depend on baseline laboratory competence and operating policies.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Technical scheduling cannot compensate for every planning or handling failure
Coding note: Human-policy constraint; should not be coded as a software defect.

Episode summary: A practitioner isolates robot subprocesses, such as lid removal, and calls the resulting checks unit tests.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Small reusable checks accelerate debugging
Coding note: Positive practice; label remains disputed.

Episode summary: Another participant argues that hardware-involved checks are functional, integration, or system tests, especially in regulated environments.
Consequence / analytical outcome: The same label is used for evidence supporting different claims
Coding note: TCA must ignore the label and code object, environment, evidence, and claim.

Episode summary: The discussion converges on reusable components with defined inputs and outputs across liquid handling, integration, and orchestration.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Modularity enables targeted tests despite incomplete early requirements
Coding note: Counterexample: community converges on a testable design principle.

Episode summary: The initiating post argues that liquid handling has a finite action vocabulary and a constrained solution space.
Consequence / analytical outcome: The method-generation problem is framed as lower-dimensional than general software
Coding note: Baseline for Context Expansion Ratio.

Episode summary: Replies enumerate rates, touch-off, droplets, viscosity, conductivity, timing, liquid classes, geometry, and biological damage.
Consequence / analytical outcome: The physically relevant option space is much larger than the action vocabulary
Coding note: Direct material-context expansion.

Episode summary: A practitioner states that human operators must feed observed physical results back into the AI after tests.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Physical feedback remains necessary for method refinement
Coding note: Separates code-generation feedback from physical feedback.

Episode summary: Participants identify sparse access to install-base data and point to community sharing as an important source of future training evidence.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Model improvement is constrained by inaccessible and non-standardized operational data
Coding note: Data availability is a modifier, not itself proof of model failure.

Episode summary: The developer reports that 92 of 100 randomly generated worklist cases produced methods whose simulation traces matched the source worklists.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Evidence supports a defined simulation-trace claim, not wet execution
Public artifact: Public test data and trace tool
Coding note: Record exact denominator, test generation process, and deepest validation stage. Not recorded as a counterexample: a product-reported result that reaches simulation depth only contradicts no construct.

Episode summary: A community reply requests AI-generated HSL unit tests runnable in a Git pipeline with simulation control.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Generation and regression coverage remain separate capabilities
Coding note: Positive community pressure toward stronger evaluation.

Episode summary: The surrounding project discussion identifies native API, complete method-artifact, and error-handling limitations beyond HSL generation.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Simulation-valid code does not constitute a complete production method system
Coding note: Use conservative wording because some limitations are addressed in later releases.

Episode summary: Users request dynamic fields and report cases where variable-volume aliquot steps are ignored in simulation without an error.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Simulation can fail to expose invalid or ignored behavior
Coding note: Explicit simulation false-negative concern.

Episode summary: Multiple users request native runtime recovery, remembered state, and the ability to resume after crashes.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Current recovery semantics are perceived as insufficient for stateful physical workflows
Coding note: Distinguish requested product capability from existing custom workarounds.

Episode summary: Requests include method versioning, JSON labware schemas, searchable logging, headless testing, and improved HSL documentation.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Users independently request separable, testable, machine-readable artifacts
Coding note: One thread contains several distinct mechanism episodes.

Episode summary: Vendor representatives participate, clarify existing capabilities, request precise examples, and route feedback to product management.
Consequence / analytical outcome: Some perceived gaps are discoverability problems; others become structured product feedback
Coding note: Important counterexample to a one-sided account of vendor closure.
